en.title: Maximum Subjects Passed Within an Extra Question Budget
en.description:
For subject i, answered[i] questions have already been answered, and passing requires at least needed[i]. You can answer at most q more questions, distributed freely; find the maximum number of subjects you can pass.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n q (1≤n≤100000, 0≤q≤10⁹), the second line contains answered, and the third line contains needed, all 0..10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: adding 25 and 27 questions passes two subjects, and the remaining 48 is not enough for the third. Example 2: the first subject is already passed, so with a budget of 0 you still pass 1 subject. Example 3: adding 2 and 3 uses up the budget exactly, and two subjects pass.
hints: The remaining cost of each subject is max(0,needed−answered); choose subjects in ascending order of cost until the budget runs out.
